rationale: Compartment syndrome ΔP<30 mmHg threshold is the key decision rule covered in the tibial plateau + compartment syndrome section
Patellar fracture management hinges on displacement threshold — covered in the management of patellar fractures block
Compartment syndrome block (index 11) explicitly covers the 'pulse present = safe' misconception that must be dispelled
Gustilo-Anderson classification and management thresholds for open tibial fractures are covered in the investigation/management block
Bohler's angle and calcaneal fracture management are core knowledge points in the calcaneus block
Lisfranc injury diagnosis — the 'fleck sign' and displacement criteria are covered in the Lisfranc block
Weber classification drives management decisions — Weber B is the critical branch point, and common errors involve treating Weber C conservatively
Syndesmotic squeeze test and Cotton test diagnosis covered in the syndesmotic injuries block
Unstable ankle fracture management and the definition of medial clear space widening drive critical management decisions
Fat embolism syndrome Gurd criteria and the classic triad (petechiae, hypoxia, confusion) are the OR known-trap covered in block 7
Blood loss estimation for closed femoral shaft fracture is a critical safety fact covered in block 4
Intramedullary nailing as definitive management and timing decisions are covered in block 9
